series.title: Kitsune Originals
series.blurb: Short illustrated stories and manga written for Kitsune: fox couriers, lantern-lit mountain towns, libraries under lakes, and four new tales of Oz.
series.rights: Text released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.

series.title: Blackwood University
series.blurb: A gothic campus musical-comedy where the stairwells bite, Mortality Services handles the paperwork, and every new student arrives with a power and a problem. Twenty screenplays, a manga chapter and the Horsemen Chronicles pilot.
series.note: Episodes 4, 8, 9, 16, 17 and 19 were written for Kitsune in the style of the series. Episode 11 isn't here yet: its file was empty. Episode 6 hasn't been added.

series.title: Incarnate · The Corruption Saga
series.blurb: A dark fantasy novel of prophecy, grief and a virus called Corruption-027. Content warning in the book: self-harm, religious themes, survivor's guilt, PTSD, trauma and adult language.

series.title: Backrooms: No Wind Resistance
series.blurb: A Backrooms script built around a music video: the yellow wallpaper of Level 0, the endless city, the Hub, and a wanderer who keeps running. Plus a prequel and spinoffs from the people around Mae: an M.E.G. officer, a B.N.T.G. trader, and a guest on Level Fun =).
series.note: The song lyrics quoted in the script aren't included; each one is marked where it appears.

works.title: Kitsu Delivers · Ch. 1: The Letter With No Name
works.label: Illustrated manga
works.blurb: A young fox courier finds a letter with no name and follows its glow all the way to the sea. A short illustrated manga.

works.title: Kitsu Delivers · Ch. 2: The Reply
works.label: Illustrated manga
works.blurb: A storm, a sleeping ferryman and a letter addressed to nobody. Kitsu carries a reply back up the mountain, and the shelf of undeliverable letters finally answers. A short illustrated manga.

works.title: Kitsu Delivers · Ch. 3: The Night Market
works.label: Illustrated manga
works.blurb: A humming parcel with a drawing of a stall, and one night a year when nine lanterns light a market above the last village. Kitsu finds the bookbinder, and a book that was holding its breath. A short illustrated manga.

works.title: The Lantern Courier
works.label: Story
works.blurb: In the mountain towns, letters travel at night. Kitsu's lantern lights the addresses, until the night it lights a letter with none.

trivia.opening: Nobody remembers who decided this. The postmaster at Hollow Pine says it was a matter of cost: the day roads belong to the ox carts and the tea merchants, and a courier who walks them must pay a toll at every bridge. The night roads belong to no one.

works.title: Winter Post
works.label: Story
works.blurb: The sequel to The Lantern Courier. Kitsu brings the lighthouse parcel home to Hollow Pine, where the stationer has died. Then the pass closes, and a letter turns up in her satchel with her own name on it.

trivia.opening: In the mountain towns, the first snow closes the high passes, and the post goes on anyway.

works.title: The Library Under the Lake
works.label: Story
works.blurb: Twenty years late, Mina returns a book to the library that was flooded to make a reservoir. The librarian, a carp in spectacles, would like a word about the fine.

trivia.opening: When they flooded the valley to make the reservoir, they moved the school, the noodle shop, the shrine and most of the graves. They did not move the library, because the library had been closed for eleven years, and because the man from the water company said that books were cheaper to replace than to carry.

works.title: Nine Umbrellas
works.label: Story
works.blurb: An old badger's umbrella shop keeps nine painted umbrellas that aren't for sale. Ask for one by name and it will take you somewhere.

trivia.opening: The old badger's umbrella shop stood at the bottom of Rain Lane, where the drainpipes of four streets all emptied into one gutter, and for that reason it was the wettest corner in the town. This was good for business. It was also why the badger, whose name was Tamba, had never in forty years owned a dry pair of socks.

works.title: The Color Thief of Oz
works.label: Story
works.blurb: Something is draining the color out of Oz, one blue lamp at a time. A Munchkin lamplighter's apprentice walks to the Emerald City to find out who, and why.

trivia.opening: In the Munchkin Country everything is blue, and nobody there has ever thought it strange. The fences are blue and the farmhouses are blue, the bonnets are blue and the cornflowers bluer still, and when a Munchkin baby first opens its eyes the cradle-quilt above it is the blue of a robin's egg, so that the world begins in that color and goes on from there.

works.title: Madison of Oz
works.label: Story
works.blurb: Madison can rewrite your memories so you think she once saved your life. In Oz it works way too easily, and finding out why rewrites the history of Oz itself.

trivia.opening: The last thing Madison Pryce did in Kansas was talk a gas station clerk out of a free iced coffee.

works.title: The Cephalotus of Oz
works.label: Story
works.blurb: A sneeze, a spilled bottle of the Powder of Life, and a tiny carnivorous pitcher plant wakes up in the Wizard's glasshouse, just as something starts eating every garden in Oz.

trivia.opening: In the glasshouse behind the Wizard's workshop in the Emerald City, among the orchids and the lemon trees and the pots of herbs that whistled when the wind was in the east, there grew a very small plant that nobody had ever paid much attention to.

works.title: The Hiccup of Oz
works.label: Story
works.blurb: The Land of Oz has the hiccups, and every hiccup swaps things around the country. A Quadling kitchen-boy who saw a star fall is the only one who knows why.

works.title: The Glass Cat of Oz
works.label: Story
works.blurb: Bungle the Glass Cat has always been the most beautiful creature in Oz, until the morning she wakes up with a crack. Glass doesn't heal. Scraps the Patchwork Girl knows someone who mends.

trivia.opening: In the Emerald City there lived a cat made entirely of glass, and she was, by her own account, the most beautiful creature in the Land of Oz.

works.title: The Night Market Bookbinder
works.label: Story
works.blurb: Pell the hedgehog mends books under a bridge at the night market, and she can hear what books remember. When Kitsu brings her one that's holding its breath, the two of them go looking for the hand that stopped writing it.

trivia.opening: The night market in Low Fennel opens when the last tram goes home, and it closes when the first gull complains about the light. In between, it sells everything a town forgets it needs: lamp wicks, mended kettles, buttons in jars sorted by mood, and, under the stone bridge where the river makes its quietest sound, books.

works.title: The Sleeper Train to Tsukimi
works.label: Story
works.blurb: On half-moon nights a train leaves from platform zero. There are no tickets: you pay with one true story. Haru missed the last train home, and the only story she has is the one she wishes she could take back.

trivia.opening: The sleeper train to Tsukimi leaves from platform zero at eleven minutes past midnight, on the nights when the moon is exactly half full.

works.title: The Weather Cartographer
works.label: Story
works.blurb: Odo the otter maps things that move: fog, frost, a drizzle that's lasted 140 years. His new apprentice, a puffin who notices everything, finds a storm on the map that isn't supposed to come for another lifetime.

trivia.opening: Everybody in the harbour town of Saltwick knew that Odo Finch made maps. What they argued about was what the maps were of.

works.title: Page Zero
works.label: Story
works.blurb: A manga artist has drawn a page a day for six years. On the first morning of the seventh, the page starts drawing back.

trivia.opening: Haru had drawn a page a day for six years, and on the first morning of the seventh year, the page drew back.

works.title: Horsemen Chronicles · Episode Three: The Seventh Floor Is Not a Floor
works.label: Prequel · Episode Three
works.blurb: The Horsemen walk into the Architect’s tower through a revolving door, meet a schedule that has Death on it since 1347, and find a seventh floor that is not a floor. Inside, a server marked Juno Pell turns into a moth. Famine offers the Architect a cookie.

sceneList.h: TOKYO BAY — DAWN — A SERVICE PIER
sceneList.f: The sea is flat and grey, the colour of an unfinished sketch. A row of container cranes stands along the horizon like a line of patient herons.
A cathedral of white marble, too clean to echo. The floor is polished so well that every footstep sounds like it is being apologised for.
A steel lift, mirror-walled. The floor counter reads: G. Above it, a row of numbers: 1 through 6, then a gap, then 7, marked in faded paint as NOT A FLOOR.

sceneList.h: ARCHITECT’S TOWER — SEVENTH FLOOR (NOT A FLOOR) — CONTINUOUS
sceneList.f: A round room, white and silent, with a single window that shows not the city but the sea, the sky, the pier, the van, and, far below, the four of them standing in the corridor looking up.
A long white corridor, lined on both sides with glass cases. Inside each case, a single small server, glowing gently, labelled with a name in white letters.
The Horsemen are walking fast. Famine is in front, chewing. Death is behind, reading out a list.
A vast, empty white room with a dome of glass. Above it, the sky is rolling with clouds that are, very slowly, forming the shapes of faces.
The chamber is quiet now. The clouds are drifting again, untroubled. The Architect has not moved from the chair.

longest.t: When you reset the timeline, you did not save one world. You saved the version of the world that you could remember. Everything else was taken down with it, in the order it was least useful to you. Trillions of realities. Your mother. Her mother. Your best friend in the other timeline who laughed at everything you said.

The campus speakers crackle.

Where the world ends. Beyond the white wall of the school, the salt-white plain, the grey sky, the nothing.

We were going to dim slowly, gracefully, for longer than there had been numbers, and it would be a long gentle sunset, and somebody would turn off the last lamp and say goodnight.

trivia.opening: Not the black of a closed eye. Something worse. A black with no edge, no floor, no distance, the black a held breath would be if it lasted forever.

sceneList.h: BLACKWOOD UNIVERSITY — THE RING ROAD — DAWN
sceneList.f: There is a road around the campus.
It thins, the way a lie thins when you walk far enough into it, and then it is gone, and Yuki stops.

sceneList.h: THE OUTSIDE — THE PETROL STATION — CONTINUOUS
sceneList.f: It comes from nowhere. It has no business existing, in a world with nothing left to move, but it comes anyway, a hard dry wail, lifting ash into long grey curtains between the two women.
A young woman in it, twenty-six, Japanese-American, dark hair cut short by someone who didn’t know how. A tray of untouched food. A window, rain on the glass.

sceneList.h: THE OUTSIDE — THE PETROL STATION — CONTINUOUS
sceneList.f: The scythe is in the ash beside her.

sceneList.h: THE OUTSIDE — THE PETROL STATION — CONTINUOUS
sceneList.f: Her hands are shaking so badly that she has to use both.
It is two women in a dead world swinging the tools of their trade at each other in a storm of ash, and neither of them wants to win.
It does not hurry. It has never needed to. Every step turns the ash white, and every white patch spreads, slowly, like frost across a window, toward the two women standing in the ruin.
The Assignor stands in the white.
It is the middle of the night. He has a mug in his hands and a blanket round his shoulders and the deeply haunted expression of a man who has been awake for two days waiting for someone.
They are standing, sitting, leaning in the doorways. Velvette, with her leather jacket slipping off one shoulder. Sasha in pyjamas, a contract still clutched in one hand. Rusk and Drake and Riggs and

longest.t: I carried every one of them. Every kid. Every boy at that petrol station. Every girl who thought she was a problem. I put them in a lifeboat and I told them it was a university because that was the only way they’d get in.

works.title: Madison, Nomad
works.label: Spinoff

sceneList.f: Fluorescent lights. One working. Two flickering. One that has given up and just hums with resentment.
Not printing. Screaming. A long, high, continuous wail, like a kettle that has seen something it cannot unsee.
Heat shimmer. Cacti. A single vulture on a single post, looking unimpressed by everything.
Madison has come back. There is nowhere else to go. The desert is very big and very empty and none of it wants to be her friend.
A black sedan with a MORTALITY SERVICES parking permit in the windshield is pulled over on the shoulder. Steam pours from under the hood.
Madison sits in the passenger seat. Yuki sits behind the wheel. Kevin floats in the back, pressed against the window, staring at a cactus with naked wonder.

A tow truck has towed the sedan to the only other building for forty miles: a diner called THE LAST STOP, which is also, according to its sign, a motel, a post office, a laundromat, and a "notary (cro
Booths. Vinyl. A jukebox that only plays songs about trucks. A waitress named BIRDIE, twenties, tattoos up both arms, chewing gum with the jaw strength of someone who has chewed through worse.
The desert sky is enormous. A billion stars. No pink spores. No friendship festival. Just sky.
Yuki puts the re-enrollment form on the Reaper's desk.

longest.t: It doesn't work anymore. The thing. My thing. I could make anybody remember anything. I could make the Dean of Blackwood think I was the best student who ever lived. works.title: Kevin Slides · Episode One: Return to Sender
works.label: Spinoff · Kevin Slides · Episode One
works.blurb: Kevin gets a sentient cardboard box from the Reaper and ten minutes to deliver it, across a graveyard of Kevins, a megachurch and a motel. Mature, heavy cussing, dark humour. Content warning: strong language, dark humour.

sceneList.f: The office is exactly as it has always been: fluorescent, damp, and one coffee short of a collapse.
White, then beige, then the particular grey of a day that has not yet decided to be a day. Kevin falls through it without making a sound, clutching the box.
He lands on a lino floor, flat on his back, box on his chest like a corpse in a cheerful casket.
A narrow stockroom. Shelves of beans labelled with names. COLUMBIA. KENYA. MARIA ODUYA. TOM REYNE. ALINA VOSS.
A wet, narrow alley between two buildings that are also Blackwood Coffee. Bins overflow with cardboard sleeves printed with the words WE ARE SORRY FOR YOUR LOSS.
Falling. The same endless beige. This time Kevin is better at it. He keeps his legs together. He holds the box with both arms. He screams only slightly.
Kevin lands on grass. Wet grass. Cold. Moonlight, thin and uninterested.
The coffin sits on the grass. The Kevins gather around it, ghostly and quiet. Smart Kevin removes the lid with the flat of his spade.
The slide this time is longer and cruder, a seasick drop through colours that don’t have names. Kevin clings to the box, shouting small apologies at the void.

sceneList.h: THE CATHEDRAL OF QUARTERLY RESULTS — SUNDAY — LATE MORNING
sceneList.f: A cathedral the size of an airport hangar, built entirely out of glass, chrome and motivational posters. Stained windows depict saints in lanyards. The pews face a giant LED screen that reads:
A narrow pipe, hot and damp, full of steam. Kevin crawls through it on his elbows, box clutched in one hand, dragging his knees on warm copper.
Falling again, but gently. As if somebody has put a hand under him.
Falling again. Kevin tucked into a ball. The Parcel clasped to his chest.
Kevin lands on his own desk. His plant, startled, sheds a leaf.
Kevin falls through the beige, box in his arms, apron-clad Yuki’s confused face fading behind him.
A long road, cracked and sun-bleached. A signpost leans in the wind. It reads WELCOME TO THE LAND OF THE LIVING.
The convertible tears down a ruler-straight road through an orange, blistered desert. Cacti stand on either side like drunken witnesses.
The convertible pulls into a gravel lot in front of a motel called THE LAST STOP, which is also, according to the neon sign, a diner, a post office, a pawn shop and a mortuary.
A small room with orange carpet, a fish tank full of dead fish, and a front desk with a bell that says PLEASE DING FOR SERVICE OR DEATH.

sceneList.h: THE LAST STOP — ROOM SIX — NIGHT
sceneList.f: The loud room. A grubby motel room that smells of cigarettes, gun oil and perfume. Blackout curtains, a neon sign outside blinking BLOOD in pink.

sceneList.h: THE LAST STOP — QUIET ROOM — NIGHT
sceneList.f: A tiny room with one bed, one lamp and one very poorly framed painting of a duck. Kevin sits on the bed, box in his lap. Outside, the neon sign blinks BLOOD in a slow, patient rhythm.
Falling. Falling gently. The box in his arms, warm as a living thing.

longest.t: Good evening, travellers. Today’s forecast: a ninety percent chance of slide. Please remember to say please. The universe is listening, and it doesn’t like rude.

works.title: Incarnate: Ember
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: After the war, the monument has one name on it. Rui, the anti-god of fire, is not that name. Then Famine starts to freeze.

trivia.opening: It stood at the center of the restored world, where the broken world had finally been sealed shut, a tower of white stone so tall that clouds snagged on it. At the top burned a flame that never went out. At the bottom, cut into the stone in letters taller than a person, was a single word.

works.title: Incarnate: Mind
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Esme, the anti-god of the mind, was a master's vessel for eleven days. A year later there's a quiet voice in her head that wants to fix everyone.

trivia.opening: Esme woke up at 4:12 in the morning with a thought in her head that was not hers.

works.title: Incarnate: Unsaid
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Pia hasn't said what she means in four years. War, the second Horseman, saves her life in a quarry, and starts forging weapons out of every argument she ever swallowed.

trivia.opening: She kept a list. Not on paper, because paper could be found. In her head.

works.title: Incarnate: Adored
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Dolly Adore has forty thousand people in love with her, one look each. Then she looks at a girl with a Horseman inside her, and the Horseman doesn't fall.

trivia.opening: Dolly Adore had forty thousand people in love with her, and she was so bored she could scream.

works.title: Incarnate: Leash
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Ivy Calder never raises her voice. Anyone who agrees with her, about anything, is bound to her. She holds eleven thousand leashes. The only one she cares about is her best friend's, and it's starting to slip.

trivia.opening: She did not need to. She had a soft, warm, reasonable voice, the voice of a favorite teacher or a very good doctor, and when she used it, people leaned in to listen. She would tilt her head.

works.title: Incarnate: Hermitage
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Who was the speechless mage at the hermitage, the year before everything ends? Once, he was a copyist in a library on Terra, and he was the first to copy the prophecy.

trivia.opening: Before he was a mage, before he lived at the edge of time, before he had lost his voice, Teodor Ashe was a copyist in a library on Terra, and he loved his job more than anything in the world.

works.title: Incarnate: Hunger
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Famine has held up the world for three years. Every night just after midnight she feels the moment she couldn't stop eating. Then Death comes down the canyon with her umbrella, and says Drake is still waiting.

trivia.opening: That was the part nobody told you about being the nexus. They told you it was an honor. They told you the whole restored world would hang from you like a coat from a hook, and that as long as you stood there in the black glass hollow at the bottom of the red canyon, nothing would fall apart.

works.title: Incarnate: Conquest
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Conquest, the first Horseman, says one word and every city kneels. Then the apocalypse happens without her, and in a tiny broken town, a nine-year-old with a paper crown stands up and asks why.

trivia.opening: That was the order. It had been the order since the very first world ended, in the very first dimension, so long ago that nobody but the Horsemen remembered it. First Conquest, on a white horse, with a crown.

works.title: Incarnate: Void
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Galactix wakes in a pocket dimension where her powers are void, and finds she isn't alone. The anti-god who started the tangling ten thousand years ago is sitting in the grey, holding a pen.

trivia.opening: That was the first thing she understood, before she understood where she was or how long she had been there. She reached for her power the way you reach for the floor when you get out of bed, without thinking, the way she had reached for it every waking moment for longer than most stars had been burning.

works.title: Incarnate: Main Character
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Calypso is cheer captain, homecoming court, and a cosmic hunger older than the planet's crust. She eats what people want. She's been saving Mark for dessert. She feels zero guilt about any of it, bestie.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains mind control, body horror, the eating of minds, manipulation, violence, and a narrator who thinks all of that is fine. She is not fine. Do not take notes from her.

works.title: Incarnate: Vessel
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Siren was born in the Nursery screaming because she knew she would die. Eri's stolen body is rotting off her. Then a human named Wren takes her in, sings her a river song, and asks what she can do to help.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains body horror, mind control, eye trauma, fear of death, manipulation of someone who trusts you, and a narrator who chooses wrong on purpose. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Relapse
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Ena tells the meetings she's forty-one days clean. It's day nine. There's a mint tin of corruption shards behind the water tank, and the night the hounds come, she has to choose who finds out.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains addiction and relapse, self-hurt themes, survivor's guilt, grief, violence, a cover-up, and a narrator who lies to you as easily as she lies to everyone else. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Experiment
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Before she was Eri, she was Himo's ninth experiment, thrown into hell. She sells the damned their own forgetting. A duke offers a way out for one bright soul, the only one who ever called her by a name.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains hell, torture, eye trauma, betrayal, the selling of a friend, experimentation, adult language, and a narrator who knows exactly what she's doing. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Static
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: A screenplay. Two weeks after the barn, Mark still has a piece of Calypso's song. He only uses it for good things. A bully. His dad. His best friend, just this once.

sceneList.f: Two weeks after the barn. Students bustle between classes. The trampoline is gone. The pudding stain on the cafeteria floor is not. It never came out.
The lunch line. Three hundred kids. Nobody quite as loud as they used to be. A lot of them stare at nothing between bites, like they're trying to remember a word.
Mark at the sink, splashing water on his face. Brad bursts in.
Small. Cluttered. Bills on the counter. A TV going in the next room. MARK'S DAD, RAY, forties, in a work shirt with a name patch, beer in hand, stands at the open fridge.
Sunlight. Ray at the stove, making pancakes. Whistling. No beer anywhere. He's wearing an apron. He has never owned an apron.
The barn on Route 9. Red paint coming off in sheets. Chalk circles still burned into the dirt outside the doors. The field around it is dead.
Posters. Gaming chair. Brad on the bed, arm still in the sling, laptop open. A knock at the window. Mark, outside, on the porch roof.
Pancakes. Apron. Whistling.
Highway. Flat country. Mark driving. The vial on its chain hangs from the rearview mirror, empty, swinging.
A big school. Clean. A banner: HOMECOMING WAS A SLAY!!! Students pour in.

longest.t: My mom. The school. Raven's mom, I don't know. Someone. Someone who can pull it out of you. Because I can't watch you turn into her, man. I watched her. I was there. I was the guy scrubbing the chalk off the doors because she told me it was a love language.

trivia.opening: Dude. You okay? You've been staring at your locker for like a full minute.

works.title: Incarnate: Chalk
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Raven wakes up to notes in her own handwriting about a boy she can't remember. The thing under the Tanner barn is hungry again, and it will make her strong enough to stop them for the price of one whole person.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains occult horror, memory loss, a missing sister, a human sacrifice, adult language, and a narrator who decides that one person is an acceptable price. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Plan B
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Himo made the corruption to end the gods. Plan A failed. Plan B needed grief, and grief needed a family with pancakes on Sundays and a girl with shining blonde hair.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains experimentation on sentient beings, the murder of parents in front of their children, manufactured grief, war, genocide, and a narrator who has never once been sorry. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Remade
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Book One from inside Mark's head, from the first "Hi Mark!" to the barn. Being under her song felt like taking off a backpack he'd worn his whole life. When Raven pulled it out, he kept one piece.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Remade A spinoff of the Corruption Saga. Book One, from inside Mark's head.

works.title: Incarnate: Main Character, Encore

works.blurb: The sequel to Main Character. Mark shows up at Calypso's new school, and she teaches him the rules. They sing the whole song at homecoming. Then Raven arrives with the barn, and Calypso does some lowkey strategic math.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Main Character, Encore A spinoff of the Corruption Saga. The sequel to Main Character.

works.title: Incarnate: Main Character, Uncut
works.label: Novel
works.blurb: A full novel told by Calypso, after Encore. Mom said come home, so she walks east: she eats a trucker, rules a whole town, goes viral, uses a Walmart as a shield, and cracks a girl who wants nothing. At the bottom of everything, Himo is waiting with Plan C. Zero character growth, babe.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Main Character, Uncut A novel of the Corruption Saga, told by Calypso. After Encore.

works.title: Incarnate: Only Child
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Noor is happy now. She has a job, a boyfriend who draws cats in foam, and no memory of why she used to be sad. Then the whole world starts humming, and she finds a room at her parents' house that says KEEP OUT. THIS MEANS NOOR.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Only Child A spinoff of the Corruption Saga. During Main Character, Uncut.

works.title: Incarnate: Wall of String
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Juniper has burned Calypso's name 912 times. She's the only one not humming. She's figured out how to make the voice of everything skip a beat. It only costs other people.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Wall of String A spinoff of the Corruption Saga. During Main Character, Uncut.

works.title: Incarnate: Last Rites
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: The song reaches Chimera on a broken highway, and it's right: she does want to end. She could break the tank with one punch. Instead she goes looking for the woman who built it.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Last Rites A spinoff of the Corruption Saga. During Main Character, Uncut.

works.title: Incarnate: Mermaid
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Hattie is eleven and the only one awake in Halcyon. Every grown-up does whatever anyone tells them, so she tells them to call her Queen. Then Juniper Vance gets off the bus with seven black candles.
chapters: Everybody in Halcyon calls me Queen Hattie.
The Dairy Queen is open every day and it's free for me.
School is cancelled, except the library, which is mine.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Mermaid A spinoff of the Corruption Saga. Halcyon, Illinois, after Calypso.

works.title: Incarnate: Best Friends
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Brad has been trapped behind his own face for eleven days, saying one sentence. When Mark dies, it lets go of him, but not all of it. And Mark's dad still says he's proud of his son to anyone who'll listen.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains mind control, being trapped in your own body, grief, the death of a best friend, a family that can't reach you, and a narrator who takes something that isn't his and calls it fixing. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Sponsor
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Marguerite runs the meetings and never shares. She bred the hounds. She was awake behind the dryer. And she knows exactly who left the blue button tin on the rubble where Ena would find it.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains addiction, enabling, war crimes, the breeding of monsters, the death of a young man, a cover-up, adult language, and a narrator who has decided that some people are tools. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Sorry
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Eri crawls to the tank on her elbows. She can't break it. Then her best friend walks in glowing red, and Eri reads every lie Ena ever told her on the roof, and decides to hand her the end of the world anyway.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains broken bodies, mind reading, the discovery of a friend's lies, addiction, enabling, revenge, adult language, and a narrator who knows exactly what she's handing her best friend and hands it over anyway. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Prophecy
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: "She will end everything. All of it." Ena has spent her whole life saying no to a sentence somebody else wrote. Now she has the song and the corruption, and the woman who wrote it is on her knees on the old highway.

trivia.opening: Trigger warning: This story contains addiction at its worst, revenge, grief inflicted on purpose, the deaths of gods, the end of everything, self-hurt themes, adult language, and a narrator who reads her own prophecy and decides to make it true. Read at your own risk.

works.title: Incarnate: Leftovers
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Calypso, on the floor of the Nursery, with almost none of her power left and a bent crown. Across the vault lies the loudest want she's ever heard: Eri's ten-thousand-year wait for two words. She's starving. She's not sorry.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Leftovers A spinoff of the Corruption Saga, told by Calypso. After Sorry, during Prophecy.

works.title: Incarnate: Margin Notes
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Himo's notebook, on the old highway. Chimera dying on the guardrail. Ena glowing in the road. And folded in the back, the original page of the prophecy, which the woman who wrote it could still edit.
chapters: The preservation of every told world.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Margin Notes A spinoff of the Corruption Saga, told by Himo. The old highway, during Prophecy.

works.title: Incarnate: Statue
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: In the city of statues in Purgatory, Tim is the one on the main square: a boy in a kitchen putting a knife into his sister. Eleven dead Sharpies, a tuna casserole, one second on a Tuesday, and whether he meant it.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Statue A spinoff of the Corruption Saga, told by Tim. Book One, from the other side of the knife.

works.title: Incarnate: Last Slice
works.label: Spinoff
works.blurb: Ena says two words and everything goes out like a party when the cops show up. Calypso sits on the guardrail and eats every last want: her mother's, the cat's, Ena's. Then she finds one more, on the other side of the page. Yours.

trivia.opening: Incarnate: Last Slice A spinoff of the Corruption Saga, told by Calypso. After Leftovers. The end.

sceneList.f: A repurposed, gutted Bank of America lobby. It looks like a warzone triage center.
The concrete tunnel vibrates violently. The roar of the approaching Flush Cycle sounds like a freight train made of liquid.
The air in the ductwork is stale, smelling of chalk dust and floor wax. It is pitch black, illuminated only by the frantic beam of Mae’s flashlight.
They slam the door. Mae jams a heavy metal filing cabinet in front of it.
The air is grey, static-charged, and smells of diesel fumes and teenage angst.
The driver’s seat is occupied by a standard ADULT FACELING in a windbreaker.
They tear out of the school lot and onto a two-lane blacktop road that stretches into a grey void.
The station is tiled in white subway bricks, coated in grime. It smells of ozone and old electricity.
The fluorescent lights are bright. Too bright.
The cafeteria is a wreck. Shattered vending machines, yellow frosting-blood smeared on the tiles, and a lingering haze of blue Liquid Pain vapor.
The alarm sirens are drowning in the maddening, fluorescent hum of the bleeding
The music swells, the synthwave echoing across an infinite, desolate landscape

longest.t: The claustrophobia is instant. They are standing in a perfectly round, six-foot-wide concrete tunnel. The walls are coated in a thick, anomalous black mold. Faint, flickering, cage-covered lightbulbs line the ceiling, casting a sickly yellow-green hue over the floating trash and floating, unrecognizable chunks of gore.

trivia.opening: The oppressive, maddening, fluorescent buzz of Level 0 fades in.[1][2]

sceneList.f: Brick tunnels. Copper pipes sweating. Sparks raining from junction boxes like sick fireworks. A roar of machinery so loud it's almost a silence.

Two years later. A concrete warehouse with fluorescent lights that flicker like they're nervous. Crates. Barrels. Stalls made of old office partitions. Wanderers in patchwork clothes haggling over Alm
Stalactites. Damp. The skittering of Deathmoths on the ceiling. Mae crawls through a narrow passage on her belly, flashlight in her teeth.

longest.t: Fuck. Okay. Okay. We can still... Those masks, the conditioning, it's reversible sometimes. If you get him somewhere quiet. Somewhere he's got a reason to come back. If he sees something that reminds him who he was—
